description: Hardcoded MySQL root password 'password' committed in local-dev docker-compose.yml; anyone reusing this compose file inherits a known root credential for the db container.
LOCAL_WP_DEBUG=true preset in .env.example; reuse of this template outside local development leaves active debug code enabled and increases error-disclosure surface.
LOCAL_WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=true preset in .env.example renders PHP errors directly to the browser; copying template outside local dev exposes paths and stack traces to users.
POP3 client opens connection with fsockopen() in plaintext with no SSL/TLS or STARTTLS option; mail server username, password and message bodies traverse the network unencrypted.
wp-mail.php passes the mailserver_pass option to POP3 over the unencrypted socket established by class-pop3.php; the configured mailbox password is transmitted cleartext on every poll.
Snoopy::_httpsrequest concatenates $this->curl_path into exec() without escapeshellarg(); a writable curl_path property would yield OS command injection when HTTPS fetch is invoked.
Deprecated Snoopy 1.2.4 (2008) HTTP client remains loadable from wp-includes despite _deprecated_file() notice; unmaintained third-party component shipped in core attack surface.
wp_hash() defaults to MD5 for hash_hmac(); weak digest used pervasively to derive nonces, scheme salts and integrity tokens, undermining cryptographic robustness over time.
wp_salt() derives the scheme salt via hash_hmac('md5', $scheme, $values['key']); broken hash primitive selected when stronger hmac algorithms (sha256, sha384) are available.
wp_check_password backward-compatibility branch validates legacy hashes via hash_equals against md5($password); MD5 remains an accepted password verifier for old accounts.
wp_generate_password fallback builds entropy as md5(uniqid(microtime().mt_rand(),true).seed); cryptographically weak PRNG, but reachable only on PHP without random_int().
wp_set_auth_cookie() calls setcookie() with positional args and no SameSite attribute; auth and logged-in cookies lack cross-site request protection beyond Secure/HttpOnly.
Plugin editor scrape_key generated as md5(rand()); rand() is not a cryptographic PRNG and yields predictable values for a security-sensitive transient identifier.
Plugin editor scrape_nonce generated as (string)rand(); insecure PRNG output used as anti-CSRF nonce for the loopback fatal-error scrape probe.
spawn_cron loopback wp_remote_post sets sslverify=>false via 'https_local_ssl_verify' default; certificate validation suppressed on the cron self-call HTTPS request.
HTTPS support fallback diagnostic invokes wp_remote_request with sslverify=>false; certificate validation disabled during the secondary HTTPS probe path.
trackback_response() echoes $error_message directly into XML <message> tag without escaping; error strings from wp_new_comment can contain input-derived fragments.
Signup form echoes WP_Error message for blogname into HTML without esc_html(); secure-by-default violation that would propagate any plugin-introduced raw input into the page.
Signup form echoes WP_Error message for blog_title into HTML without esc_html(); output relies on upstream sanitization rather than output-time escaping.
Signup form echoes WP_Error message for user_name without esc_html(); output sink unsafe by default if any filter or plugin re-introduces raw input into the error text.
Signup form echoes WP_Error message for user_email without esc_html(); the email field's error text is rendered unsanitized at the output boundary.
Signup form echoes WP_Error message for generic error without esc_html(); generic error channel can carry arbitrary plugin-supplied text into rendered HTML.
wp_authenticate_username_password returns distinct WP_Error codes (invalid_username vs incorrect_password) revealing whether a username exists; enables account enumeration.
maybe_unserialize() invokes @unserialize(trim($data)) on stored option/meta values; if attacker can write serialized payload (e.g. via SQLi), enables PHP object injection.
wp_generator() emits the generator meta tag containing the WordPress version; aids fingerprinting and targeted version-specific exploit selection by remote attackers.
get_allowed_http_origins() permits both http:// and https:// variants of admin/home hosts; weakens cross-origin policy on HTTPS-only sites and accepts insecure origin scheme.
PHPass random pool fallback constructs entropy via md5(microtime().random_state) and md5(random_state, true); cryptographically weak when /dev/urandom and openssl unavailable.
DOMDocument::loadXML() consumes oEmbed XML response with no LIBXML_NONET option set; doctype is checked after parsing, allowing entity processing on PHP versions before defaults hardened.
